processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was fabricated using a high-frequency vacuum induction melting furnace.
Hot-forged into billets with a thickness of 110 mm at 1150 °C and then air cooling to room temperature.
The hot-forged billets were initially reheated at 1150 °C before hot rolling.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 60 mm corresponding to a hot-rolling reduction of 45%; the number of passes was 4 for the HR45 sample.
After hot rolling the plates were water quenched to room temperature; the fast cooling produced κ-carbides without further aging.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic microstructure consisting of equiaxed FCC austenite grains with a large fraction of first-order annealing twins (Σ3 <111> 60° grain boundaries); micron-sized polygonal (Nb,Mo,W)C stringers, homogeneously dispersed submicron spherical (Nb,Mo,W)C particles, and nano-sized κ-carbides inside the austenite grains.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with abundant first-order annealing twins (Σ3, 60°<111>)
phases_present.grain_size: 45.11 μm (mean austenite grain size, excluding twin boundaries; effective grain size including twin boundaries 21.82 μm)

phases_present.morphology: nano-sized particles homogeneously precipitated inside the austenite grains during water quenching (dark-field speckle)

phases_present.crystal_structure: face-centered cubic (FCC), MC-type complex carbide; lattice parameter 4.36 Å
phases_present.morphology: two populations — micron-sized polygonal particles (sizes ranging 1 to 25 μm) distributed along the rolling direction in grain boundaries and grain interiors; submicron-sized spherical particles distributed homogeneously in the austenite matrix

defects.type: geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) / local strain concentration

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: effective grain size including annealing twin boundaries = 21.82 μm
grain_structure.texture: no strong texture reported; Σ3 (60°<111>) annealing twin boundaries account for 67% of the boundaries with misorientation >15°

precipitates.distribution: homogeneously precipitated inside the austenite grains
homogeneously distributed in the austenite matrix (submicron spherical particles)
precipitates.coherency: incoherent, bypassed by dislocations via Orowan mechanism

precipitates.distribution: micron-sized polygonal particles distributed along the rolling direction in the grain boundary and grain interior

structures.overall_structure: Deformation substructures formed by predominant dislocation planar glide after interrupted tensile tests at engineering strains of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4 — planar slip bands, Taylor lattice, and microbands.

phases_present.morphology: arrays of planar slip bands distributed homogeneously within the austenite matrix; Taylor lattice formed by intersections of two non-coplanar {111} slip traces
more closely spaced slip bands than at εe = 0.1
microbands with ill-defined and distinct boundaries

defects.type: microbands delineated by dislocation walls consisting of GNDs

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent; sheared by dislocations generating anti-phase boundaries (APBs)
incoherent; dislocations bypass via Orowan mechanism; strain/stress concentration at interfaces due to deformation discrepancy

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Shearing of κ-carbides by leading dislocations produces APBs and generates a preferential glide path (glide plane softening), leading to planar slip bands and Taylor lattice formation.
Dislocations bypass incoherent (Nb,Mo,W)C particles via the Orowan mechanism; strengthening contribution 6.5 MPa for HR45.

Intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles act as preferential nucleation sites for microcracks; strain/stress concentration partially alleviated by debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and microvoid formation. Intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles virtually played no detrimental effect on toughness.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Predominant dislocation planar glide; planar slip bands refining with strain and evolving into microbands; Taylor lattice formed by intersection of two non-coplanar {111} slip traces. For HR45 the slip band spacing at εe = 0.1 was 296.40 ± 50.06 nm, refining to ~50 nm at higher strains.
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides with L′12-type structure were produced by spinodal decomposition and subsequent ordering reaction during fast cooling (water quenching) without a further aging process.
interfaces.interface_notes: The HR45 sample (coarser grains) showed microbands only at higher strains; microbands were observed at εe = 0.2 in HR68 and HR82, indicating faster substructure development with finer grain size.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile sample cut along the rolling direction (RD), gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests on an MTS tensile machine; extensometer applied

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress (σe)-strain (εe) curve of HR45 (lowest of three curves), peaks between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines near εe ≈ 0.50 and extends to about εe ≈ 0.63.
tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: Three-staged strain-hardening behavior; strain-hardening rate maintained at a high level of ~2000 MPa over a wide plastic strain range; stage II shows a gradual increase to peak values.
